U.S. Stocks Trend (Oct 14): JPMorgan Misses Profit Expectations, Apple Launches $299 HomeView | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto News项目动态U.S. Stocks Trend (Oct 14): JP...U.S. Stocks Trend (Oct 14): JPMorgan Misses Profit Expectations, Apple Launches $299 HomeViewmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-14Last updated on 2026-10-14AbstractU.S. Stock Market Trend (Oct 14): JPMorgan Misses Profit Expectations, Apple Launches $299 HomeView

U.S. stock indices closed slightly lower on Tuesday as the start of earnings season failed to boost the market. JPMorgan's profits fell short of expectations, while Citigroup and Wells Fargo also faced selling pressure after reporting results. Chip stocks initially declined but recovered most losses by the close, though Micron and Applied Materials finished notably lower. Apple officially launched its HomeView smart home device; its stock initially rose but closed with only a marginal gain. Market focus now shifts to the upcoming September U.S. CPI data, which will test expectations for a pause in rate hikes this month.

The S&P 500 dipped 0.02%, the Nasdaq fell 0.15%, and the Dow Jones declined 0.35%. Sector performance was mixed: Energy, Communication Services, and Utilities rose, while Healthcare and Financials fell. Among the "Magnificent Seven," Meta and Nvidia gained, while Amazon and Tesla declined.

Despite reporting profit growth, major banks saw their stocks fall. JPMorgan's Q3 EPS of $5.57 missed estimates of around $5.90. Investment securities losses were a drag. Goldman Sachs' results were solid, but its stock still edged lower. Wells Fargo and Citigroup dropped more sharply on net interest income concerns, highlighting investor scrutiny of revenue mix and forward guidance.

It argues this isn't a typical altcoin season driven by broad FOMO, but a more selective shift. The rally is attributed to these projects being fully (or nearly) unlocked from vesting schedules and having legitimate, renewed technological narratives. Examples include ZEC's privacy focus and Starknet's "quantum-resistant" narrative, which gained traction following concerns about quantum computing potentially breaking current cryptography. The author suggests this represents a key paradigm shift for experienced investors, moving away from chasing short-term pumps towards valuing established projects with real utility and unlocked supply. Morgan Stanley Report Interpretation: Samsung's Profit Ranks First Globally, Storage Supercycle Struggles to Gain Full Valuation | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto News比特币Morgan Stanley Report Interpre...Morgan Stanley Report Interpretation: Samsung's Profit Ranks First Globally, Storage Supercycle Struggles to Gain Full ValuationmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-13Last updated on 2026-10-13AbstractMorgan Stanley Research Report Analysis: Samsung Leads in Global Profits, But Storage Supercycle Fails to Secure Full Valuation

Samsung Electronics posted an operating profit of approximately $81.3 billion in Q3 2026, surpassing Nvidia's $71.6 billion to become the world's most profitable company. Despite this, Samsung and SK Hynix shares have fallen 35% from their peaks, trading at forward P/E ratios of just 3-4x. Morgan Stanley's October 2026 report argues that while a structural AI-driven storage supercycle is real, the market refuses to pay full valuation for record earnings, still pricing these stocks within a traditional boom-bust cycle framework.

AI data center demand is the primary driver, with the HBM market projected to triple to $100 billion by 2028. Long-term contracts with price floors have altered industry risk profiles. However, Morgan Stanley emphasizes that a supercycle does not mean the end of cyclicality; new supply will eventually catch up, potentially ending the cycle around 2027 or later.

The report notes that AI is reshaping storage demand structure, with HBM physically crowding out standard DRAM capacity. China's Yangtze Memory and CXMT are also cited as important variables in the global supply landscape.

Morgan Stanley recommends a strategic shift in portfolio allocation: underweighting storage selectively while overweighting AI computing (e.g., Nvidia, TSMC) and network supply chains. bonuses.requirements: Citigroup: Aave Poised to Become a Decentralized Collateral Liquidity Protocol Connecting Tokenized Assets and FinancingHomeFeedNewsCitigroup: Aave Poised to Become a Decentralized Collateral Liquidity Protocol Connecting Tokenized Assets and FinancingCitigroup: Aave Poised to Become a Decentralized Collateral Liquidity Protocol Connecting Tokenized Assets and Financing10/20 02:40On October 20, Citigroup Research released a report stating that viewing Aave solely as a crypto-native lending protocol is no longer sufficient. As tokenized assets, stablecoins, and institutional participation gradually enter mainstream finance, Aave is expected to be positioned as a decentralized collateral liquidity protocol. Projects such as Aave V4, Horizon, and GHO point towards the intersection of collateral, liquidity, and financing. The report highlights that if tokenization determines which assets enter the blockchain, and stablecoins become the default settlement basis, Aave could help decide how these assets are financed, leveraged, used as collateral, and integrated into capital markets. Citigroup believes that as tokenization expands from stablecoins to money market funds, private credit, government bonds, and even future equities, the circulation of collateral may ultimately become one of the most important application scenarios for tokenization. Aave provides a practical case demonstrating how tokenized assets can be used for collateralized borrowing, financing, and re-collateralization within the digital financial system, offering insights into the future of tokenized capital markets, securities financing, and even prime brokerage.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HTX does not provide any trading recommendations.。Related ArticlesAave Governance Approves Base Parameter Update For v3 Markets$10 mln in AAVE inflows signal a potential breakout – What’s next for price?AAVE Builds Momentum: Is a Move to $120 Within Reach or W

The stablecoin ranks second in market capitalization: $73 billion versus $184 billion for Tether USDt.The 'significant' status comes at a time when many EU-based token issuers have been striving for regulated, dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. SK Hynix and Samsung have fallen over 50% from their June peaks, leaving them at just 2-3x 2027-28E consensus EPS—below the 4-7x seen in prior upcycles and near 1.0x 2027-28E book value, levels historically seen only at cycle bottoms. BofA maintains supercycle-level earnings forecasts: 2028 EPS declines only single digits YoY, with sales, operating profit and EPS still near 2027 peaks and record highs. So valuation prices a bottom while earnings show no downturn.

SK Hynix fell 57% from June to October, exceeding its 20-year average 51% drawdown, but in only 4 months versus the historical 15. Current DRAM ASPs are up 20-30% YoY, versus the 10-30% declines typical at bottoms. AI data center demand—LPDDR5, SOCAMM, HBM and eSSD—plus rising memory content per GPU/ASIC continues to drive growth.

Investor feedback is split: hedge funds bearish, most long-only investors bullish, with disagreement focused on cycle length rather than direction. Bear cases include neocloud borrowing costs, China 4F2 DRAM supply, falling memory per GPU, and slower AI capex. BofA rebuts each: valuations remain too low, China 4F2 impact is limited, AI backlog is large, and margins and ROIC stay high. Shareholder returns via dividends and buybacks could exceed 10% of market cap in 2027-28. BofA sees the storage TAM growing from ~$1.0tn in 2026 to over $2.0tn by 2030.
